programme.displayName: Build and Test Your First AWS Lambda Function
programme.subtitle: Build, invoke, expose, version, monitor, and clean up an intermediate Node.js Lambda workload
programme.description: Create a least-privilege training identity, a Node.js Lambda function, Amazon SQS event processing with a dead-letter queue, an Amazon API Gateway HTTP API, a published Lambda version and alias, structured CloudWatch Logs, and a no-notification CloudWatch alarm. The lab uses only harmless fixed sample data in Europe (London), eu-west-2.
programme.learningOutcome: You can build and test a Lambda function through direct invocation, an HTTP API, and an SQS event source mapping; diagnose successful and failed processing through CloudWatch Logs and metrics; understand versions and aliases; and remove the complete training environment safely.

phases.title: Prepare secure training access
phases.description: Create a dedicated non-root IAM user, attach a training policy, create one temporary access key, and configure the named AWS CLI profile.

phases.title: Build the Lambda processing foundation
phases.description: Create the execution role, source queue, dead-letter queue, managed log group, and Node.js Lambda function.

phases.title: Invoke Lambda through synchronous, HTTP, and queue-driven paths
phases.description: Test direct invocation, expose the function through API Gateway HTTP API, and process successful and intentionally failing SQS messages.

phases.title: Release, observe, and troubleshoot the workload
phases.description: Publish an immutable Lambda version, create an alias, inspect structured logs, and create a CloudWatch error alarm.

phases.title: Remove the training environment
phases.description: Delete every named resource in reverse dependency order and verify that no chargeable or security-sensitive training resource remains.

tasks.title: Create the dedicated training identity and CLI profile
tasks.feature: IAM least privilege and AWS CLI
tasks.goal: Create fa-lambda-intermediate-user with temporary Console and CLI access, attach fa-lambda-intermediate-policy, create one temporary access key, and configure the fa-lambda-intermediate profile for eu-west-2.
tasks.whyItMatters: Use a dedicated non-root identity for this lab. The policy permits Lambda, API Gateway, SQS, logging, and monitoring work, and permits IAM operations only for the named Lambda execution role that the lab creates and passes to Lambda.

consoleSteps.title: Record the account ID and create the training user
consoleSteps.instruction: Sign in using an existing administrator identity. Do not use the root user unless the account has no administrator identity.

instructions.text: Sign in using an existing administrator identity. Do not use the root user unless the account has no administrator identity.
In the AWS console header, choose the account name or account number menu.
Record the 12-digit AWS account ID as <ACCOUNT_ID>. You will replace this placeholder in the policy in the next step.
In the navigation pane, choose Users.
Select Provide user access to the AWS Management Console.
Choose I want to create an IAM user.
Enter a unique temporary password that you can safely use once.
Select Users must create a new password at next sign-in.
Do not add permissions on this page; choose Next.
Review the user name and choose Create user.
Record the IAM user sign-in URL shown on the success page.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: fa-lambda-intermediate-user exists, can sign in through the recorded IAM user URL, and has no permissions yet.
consoleSteps.warning: Do not create root access keys. Do not share the temporary password or the IAM user sign-in URL.

consoleSteps.title: Create the restricted training policy
consoleSteps.instruction: In IAM, choose Policies in the navigation pane.

instructions.text: In IAM, choose Policies in the navigation pane.
Replace all existing editor content with the complete policy shown below.
Replace <ACCOUNT_ID> with the 12-digit account ID recorded in the previous step. Do not change any resource names.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: The customer managed policy fa-lambda-intermediate-policy exists.
consoleSteps.warning: This is a scoped training policy, not a production authorization design. It allows IAM management only for fa-lambda-intermediate-execution-role.

consoleSteps.title: Attach the policy and create the temporary access key
consoleSteps.instruction: Choose Users in the IAM navigation pane.

instructions.text: Choose Users in the IAM navigation pane.
In Access keys, choose Create access key.
Download the CSV file once and store it securely until the CLI profile is configured.
Sign out of the administrator session.
Use the recorded IAM user sign-in URL to sign in as fa-lambda-intermediate-user and set the required new password.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: The training user has fa-lambda-intermediate-policy attached, one access key identified by [LAB_ACCESS_KEY_ID], and working non-root Console access.
consoleSteps.warning: The secret access key appears only once. Never paste it into code, user data, logs, screenshots, source control, or notes.

cliSteps.explanation: Run this command using an existing administrator profile. IAM is global, so --region is intentionally omitted.
cliSteps.warning: Replace <ADMIN_PROFILE> with a pre-existing administrator CLI profile; do not use root credentials.

cliSteps.explanation: Replace <ACCOUNT_ID> with the 12-digit account ID and <ADMIN_PROFILE> with the existing administrator profile. Record the returned Policy.Arn as [LAB_POLICY_ARN].
cliSteps.expectedResult: The response contains the ARN of fa-lambda-intermediate-policy.
cliSteps.warning: IAM is global, so --region is intentionally omitted.

cliSteps.explanation: Attach the policy created in the preceding CLI step only to fa-lambda-intermediate-user.
cliSteps.warning: Replace [LAB_POLICY_ARN] with the exact policy ARN returned by create-policy.

cliSteps.explanation: Record AccessKey.AccessKeyId as [LAB_ACCESS_KEY_ID]. Use SecretAccessKey only at the next aws configure prompt; it is returned once.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The response contains AccessKeyId and SecretAccessKey.
cliSteps.warning: Do not save SecretAccessKey in a shell history, file, screenshot, or course notes.

cliSteps.explanation: At the prompts, enter the access key and one-time secret from create-access-key, enter eu-west-2 as Default region name, and enter json as Default output format.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The local AWS CLI stores the fa-lambda-intermediate profile.
cliSteps.warning: This command writes credentials to the local AWS shared credentials file.

cliSteps.explanation: Confirm the account and ARN used by the training profile before creating regional resources.
cliSteps.warning: Stop if the returned user or account is not the intended training identity.

verification.title: Confirm Console identity and policy attachment
verification.instruction: Sign in through the recorded IAM user sign-in URL as fa-lambda-intermediate-user. In IAM, open the user's Permissions tab.
verification.expectedResult: The signed-in identity is fa-lambda-intermediate-user and fa-lambda-intermediate-policy is attached.

verification.title: Confirm CLI identity
verification.instruction: Inspect the Arn returned by aws sts get-caller-identity.
verification.expectedResult: The ARN identifies fa-lambda-intermediate-user.

tasks.title: Create the Lambda execution role
tasks.goal: Create fa-lambda-intermediate-execution-role and attach AWSLambdaSQSQueueExecutionRole before creating the function.
tasks.whyItMatters: Lambda assumes its execution role when it runs. AWSLambdaSQSQueueExecutionRole grants the queue read and delete permissions needed for the SQS event source mapping and the CloudWatch Logs permissions needed for function logging.

consoleSteps.title: Create the Lambda service role

instructions.text: Record the Role ARN as [LAMBDA_ROLE_ARN] from the role Summary section.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: The named role exists and has AWSLambdaSQSQueueExecutionRole attached.
consoleSteps.warning: The trusted service must be Lambda. Do not attach this role to a person or another service.

cliSteps.explanation: Create the execution role with a trust policy that allows only the Lambda service principal to assume it. Record the returned Role.Arn as [LAMBDA_ROLE_ARN].
cliSteps.expectedResult: The response contains the role ARN for fa-lambda-intermediate-execution-role.
cliSteps.warning: IAM is global, so this command intentionally has no --region.

cliSteps.explanation: Attach the AWS managed policy that permits SQS polling and CloudWatch Logs writes.
cliSteps.warning: IAM is global, so this command intentionally has no --region.

verification.title: Confirm the trust relationship
verification.instruction: Open the Trust relationships tab for fa-lambda-intermediate-execution-role.
verification.expectedResult: The trust policy names lambda.amazonaws.com as the service principal.

verification.title: Confirm queue and log permissions
verification.instruction: Open the Permissions tab for fa-lambda-intermediate-execution-role.
verification.expectedResult: AWSLambdaSQSQueueExecutionRole is attached.

tasks.title: Create the source queue and dead-letter queue
tasks.goal: Create a standard source queue and a standard DLQ, then configure the source queue to move a repeatedly failing message to the DLQ after two receives.
tasks.whyItMatters: Lambda processes SQS messages at least once. A failed batch can be delivered again, so handlers should be idempotent. The DLQ retains messages that continue to fail instead of leaving them indefinitely in the source queue.

consoleSteps.title: Create the standard dead-letter queue

instructions.text: Leave the remaining settings at their defaults.
Record the Queue ARN in the Details section as [DLQ_ARN].

consoleSteps.expectedResult: The standard dead-letter queue exists and its ARN is recorded as [DLQ_ARN].
consoleSteps.warning: Use a standard queue for both queues in this lab. A FIFO queue can use only a FIFO DLQ.

consoleSteps.title: Create and configure the standard source queue

instructions.text: Record the Queue URL in the Details section as [SOURCE_QUEUE_URL].
Record the Queue ARN in the Details section as [SOURCE_QUEUE_ARN].

consoleSteps.expectedResult: The source queue has a 120-second visibility timeout and redrives messages to the named DLQ after two receives.
consoleSteps.warning: The visibility timeout must be longer than the Lambda timeout. Do not inspect the failing message repeatedly in the SQS console because viewing a message can count toward its receive count.

cliSteps.command: aws sqs create-queue --queue-name fa-lambda-intermediate-dlq --profile fa-lambda-intermediate --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: Record the QueueUrl response field as [DLQ_URL].
cliSteps.expectedResult: The response contains the URL of fa-lambda-intermediate-dlq.
cliSteps.warning: Use the same Region as the Lambda function.

cliSteps.command: aws sqs get-queue-attributes --queue-url [DLQ_URL] --attribute-names QueueArn --query Attributes.QueueArn --output text --profile fa-lambda-intermediate --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: Record the output as [DLQ_ARN].
cliSteps.expectedResult: The output is the ARN of fa-lambda-intermediate-dlq.
cliSteps.warning: Replace [DLQ_URL] with the URL returned by create-queue.

cliSteps.command: aws sqs create-queue --queue-name fa-lambda-intermediate-source --attributes VisibilityTimeout=120 --profile fa-lambda-intermediate --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: Record the QueueUrl response field as [SOURCE_QUEUE_URL].
cliSteps.expectedResult: The response contains the URL of fa-lambda-intermediate-source.
cliSteps.warning: The 120-second visibility timeout gives a failed message time to become visible again for the deliberate retry exercise.

cliSteps.command: aws sqs get-queue-attributes --queue-url [SOURCE_QUEUE_URL] --attribute-names QueueArn --query Attributes.QueueArn --output text --profile fa-lambda-intermediate --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: Record the output as [SOURCE_QUEUE_ARN].
cliSteps.expectedResult: The output is the ARN of fa-lambda-intermediate-source.
cliSteps.warning: Replace [SOURCE_QUEUE_URL] with the URL returned by create-queue.

cliSteps.explanation: Associate the source queue with the existing DLQ and set the maximum receive count to 2.
cliSteps.warning: Replace [SOURCE_QUEUE_URL] and [DLQ_ARN] only with values created in this lab.

verification.title: Confirm the queue pairing
verification.instruction: Open fa-lambda-intermediate-source and inspect its Dead-letter queue configuration.
verification.expectedResult: fa-lambda-intermediate-dlq is selected and Maximum receives is 2.

verification.title: Confirm same-Region placement
verification.instruction: Inspect the source and DLQ ARNs.
verification.expectedResult: Both ARNs contain eu-west-2.

tasks.title: Create the managed log group and Lambda function
tasks.goal: Create a seven-day CloudWatch log group and deploy fa-lambda-intermediate-processor with Node.js 24.x, JSON logging, and the named Lambda execution role.
tasks.whyItMatters: Creating the log group before invocation makes retention explicit. The function writes harmless structured logs and supports the direct, HTTP API, and SQS event shapes used later in the lab.

consoleSteps.title: Create the retained log group
consoleSteps.instruction: Open the CloudWatch console in Europe (London).

instructions.text: Open the CloudWatch console in Europe (London).
In the navigation pane, choose Log groups.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: The log group /aws/lambda/fa-lambda-intermediate-processor exists with seven-day retention.
consoleSteps.warning: CloudWatch Logs storage can incur charges. Final cleanup deletes only this exact log group.

consoleSteps.title: Create and deploy the Node.js function
consoleSteps.instruction: Open the Lambda console in Europe (London).

instructions.text: Open the Lambda console in Europe (London).
On the Code tab, open index.mjs.
Replace all file content with the complete index.mjs source below.
Choose Deploy and wait for the deployment success message.

jsonBlocks.title: index.mjs

consoleSteps.expectedResult: The Lambda function is deployed with the named execution role and the supplied handler.
consoleSteps.warning: Do not put credentials, secrets, personal data, or production business logic in this training code.

consoleSteps.title: Configure JSON logging
consoleSteps.instruction: Open the Configuration tab for fa-lambda-intermediate-processor.

instructions.text: Open the Configuration tab for fa-lambda-intermediate-processor.
For Application log level, select INFO.
For System log level, select INFO.
Wait until the configuration update completes.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: The function is configured to write JSON logs to the precreated log group.
consoleSteps.warning: AWSLambdaSQSQueueExecutionRole already supplies the required CloudWatch Logs write permissions.

cliSteps.explanation: Create the exact log group before the function is invoked.
cliSteps.warning: Do not create a differently named log group.

cliSteps.explanation: Set the training log group's retention period to seven days.
cliSteps.warning: Final cleanup deletes the complete named log group.

cliSteps.explanation: In a Bash-compatible terminal, run this one command. Paste the complete index.mjs source from this task's JSON block, then press Ctrl+D on a new empty line to finish writing the file. This step performs only the local source-file creation operation.
cliSteps.expectedResult: A local file named index.mjs exists in the current directory.
cliSteps.warning: Do not proceed to the ZIP command until the file has been closed with Ctrl+D and contains the complete supplied training code.

cliSteps.explanation: Create a ZIP deployment package containing the index.mjs file created in the preceding step.
cliSteps.expectedResult: A local function.zip archive exists in the current directory.
cliSteps.warning: Run this only after index.mjs has been created successfully.

cliSteps.command: aws lambda create-function --function-name fa-lambda-intermediate-processor --runtime nodejs24.x --role [LAMBDA_ROLE_ARN] --handler index.handler --zip-file fileb://function.zip --timeout 10 --memory-size 128 --architectures x86_64 --profile fa-lambda-intermediate --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: Create the function. [LAMBDA_ROLE_ARN] is the Role ARN recorded when task 2 created fa-lambda-intermediate-execution-role. Record FunctionArn from the response as [FUNCTION_ARN].
cliSteps.expectedResult: The response contains FunctionName fa-lambda-intermediate-processor and FunctionArn.
cliSteps.warning: Use the exact role ARN from this lab, not a role name or an unrelated role.

cliSteps.command: aws lambda wait function-active-v2 --function-name fa-lambda-intermediate-processor --profile fa-lambda-intermediate --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: Wait until the function is active before modifying its configuration.
cliSteps.warning: Stop and inspect the function if Lambda reports a failed state.

cliSteps.command: aws lambda update-function-configuration --function-name fa-lambda-intermediate-processor --logging-config LogFormat=JSON,ApplicationLogLevel=INFO,SystemLogLevel=INFO,LogGroup=/aws/lambda/fa-lambda-intermediate-processor --profile fa-lambda-intermediate --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: Configure JSON application and system logs in the log group created in CLI step 1.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The response contains the requested LoggingConfig values.
cliSteps.warning: Wait for this configuration update to complete before publishing a Lambda version.

verification.title: Confirm function configuration
verification.instruction: Open fa-lambda-intermediate-processor in Lambda and inspect Configuration, Runtime settings, and Permissions.
verification.expectedResult: Runtime is Node.js 24.x and the execution role is fa-lambda-intermediate-execution-role.

verification.title: Confirm the explicit log destination
verification.instruction: Inspect Monitoring and operations tools in the function configuration.
verification.expectedResult: Log format is JSON and Log group is /aws/lambda/fa-lambda-intermediate-processor.

tasks.title: Run a direct synchronous test
tasks.goal: Invoke the deployed function with fixed dimensions and confirm that it returns an area of 42.
tasks.whyItMatters: A direct test isolates the handler from API Gateway and SQS. It confirms the event contract, response, and basic CloudWatch logging before integrations are added.

consoleSteps.title: Create the direct invocation test event
consoleSteps.instruction: Open the Test tab for fa-lambda-intermediate-processor.

instructions.text: Open the Test tab for fa-lambda-intermediate-processor.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: A saved test event named direct-area-test contains the two harmless numeric values.
consoleSteps.warning: Use only the fixed sample input. Do not enter passwords, tokens, access keys, or personal data.

consoleSteps.title: Invoke the direct test event

instructions.text: Open the execution result Details section.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: The invocation succeeds and returns a response body containing area 42.
consoleSteps.warning: If the test fails, inspect index.mjs and deploy the corrected code before continuing.

cliSteps.command: aws lambda invoke --function-name fa-lambda-intermediate-processor --cli-binary-format raw-in-base64-out --payload '{"length":6,"width":7}' direct-area-response.json --profile fa-lambda-intermediate --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: Synchronously invoke the function with the harmless event. The function response is written to the local direct-area-response.json file.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The command response contains StatusCode 200 and the local response file contains area 42.
cliSteps.warning: This command creates a local response file, not an AWS resource.

verification.title: Confirm the calculation
verification.instruction: Inspect the Console response or direct-area-response.json.
verification.expectedResult: The returned JSON body contains area 42.

verification.title: Confirm the direct invocation log
verification.instruction: Open the function Monitor tab and choose View CloudWatch logs.
verification.expectedResult: A recent log stream contains a JSON message with Area calculated and area 42.

tasks.title: Create an HTTP API integration
tasks.goal: Create an HTTP API with a Lambda proxy integration, a GET /area route, a lab stage, and a Lambda resource-policy permission for API Gateway.
tasks.whyItMatters: API Gateway provides an HTTP endpoint in front of Lambda. The Lambda resource policy authorizes API Gateway, while the route and integration decide which HTTP requests invoke the function.

consoleSteps.title: Create the HTTP API and Lambda integration

instructions.text: Record the API ID as [HTTP_API_ID] from the API details page.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: The API exists with a Lambda integration for fa-lambda-intermediate-processor.
consoleSteps.warning: When the Lambda integration is created in the API Gateway console, API Gateway automatically configures Lambda invocation permission.

consoleSteps.title: Create the GET route and lab stage
consoleSteps.instruction: Choose Routes in the API navigation pane.

instructions.text: Choose Routes in the API navigation pane.
Select the Lambda integration for fa-lambda-intermediate-processor.
Choose Stages in the API navigation pane.
Record the Invoke URL shown for the lab stage as [HTTP_API_INVOKE_URL].

consoleSteps.expectedResult: GET /area is deployed to the lab stage and its invoke URL is recorded.
consoleSteps.warning: This lab uses an unauthenticated temporary endpoint. Do not use it for confidential or production workloads.

consoleSteps.title: Test the HTTP endpoint
consoleSteps.expectedResult: The endpoint returns a JSON body containing Lambda HTTP endpoint is working and the /area path.
consoleSteps.warning: Use the exact invoke URL recorded on the API Gateway stage page.

cliSteps.command: aws apigatewayv2 create-api --name fa-lambda-intermediate-http-api --protocol-type HTTP --profile fa-lambda-intermediate --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: Create an empty HTTP API. Record ApiId as [HTTP_API_ID].
cliSteps.expectedResult: The response contains the API ID and name fa-lambda-intermediate-http-api.
cliSteps.warning: Do not use a REST API for this specific lab.

cliSteps.command: aws apigatewayv2 create-integration --api-id [HTTP_API_ID] --integration-type AWS_PROXY --integration-uri arn:aws:apigateway:eu-west-2:lambda:path/2015-03-31/functions/[FUNCTION_ARN]/invocations --payload-format-version 2.0 --profile fa-lambda-intermediate --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: Create the HTTP API Lambda proxy integration. Record IntegrationId as [HTTP_INTEGRATION_ID].
cliSteps.expectedResult: The response contains the new integration ID.
cliSteps.warning: Replace [FUNCTION_ARN] with the unqualified Lambda function ARN recorded in task 4.

cliSteps.command: aws apigatewayv2 create-route --api-id [HTTP_API_ID] --route-key 'GET /area' --target integrations/[HTTP_INTEGRATION_ID] --profile fa-lambda-intermediate --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: Create the GET /area route. Record RouteId as [HTTP_ROUTE_ID].
cliSteps.warning: Replace both placeholders with values returned by this task.

cliSteps.command: aws apigatewayv2 create-stage --api-id [HTTP_API_ID] --stage-name lab --auto-deploy --profile fa-lambda-intermediate --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: Create an automatically deployed lab stage. Record the InvokeUrl as [HTTP_API_INVOKE_URL].
cliSteps.expectedResult: The response contains StageName lab and an InvokeUrl.
cliSteps.warning: The stage is regional and must be created in eu-west-2.

cliSteps.command: aws lambda add-permission --function-name fa-lambda-intermediate-processor --statement-id fa-lambda-intermediate-apigw-invoke --action lambda:InvokeFunction --principal apigateway.amazonaws.com --source-arn arn:aws:execute-api:eu-west-2:<ACCOUNT_ID>:[HTTP_API_ID]/lab/GET/area --profile fa-lambda-intermediate --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: Allow only the GET /area route in the named lab stage of this HTTP API to invoke the function.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The response contains a Lambda resource-policy statement.
cliSteps.warning: Replace <ACCOUNT_ID> and [HTTP_API_ID] with this lab's exact values.

cliSteps.command: aws apigatewayv2 get-stage --api-id [HTTP_API_ID] --stage-name lab --query InvokeUrl --output text --profile fa-lambda-intermediate --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: Record the output as [HTTP_API_INVOKE_URL]. Append /area in a browser to test the route.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The output is the invoke URL for the lab stage.
cliSteps.warning: The CLI command reads the stage only; it does not invoke the endpoint.

verification.title: Confirm API Gateway permission scope
verification.instruction: Open the Lambda Permissions tab and inspect the resource-based policy statement.
verification.expectedResult: The statement ID is fa-lambda-intermediate-apigw-invoke and the principal is apigateway.amazonaws.com.

verification.title: Confirm HTTP invocation
verification.instruction: Open [HTTP_API_INVOKE_URL]/area in a browser.
verification.expectedResult: The response is JSON from the Lambda HTTP event branch.

tasks.title: Create the SQS trigger and exercise success and failure behavior
tasks.feature: Lambda SQS event source mapping and DLQ
tasks.goal: Connect the source queue to Lambda, process one successful message, then send the fixed fail message and observe it reach the DLQ.
tasks.whyItMatters: Lambda polls SQS and invokes the function synchronously with a batch. A successful batch is deleted. A thrown error makes the message visible again after the visibility timeout; after the configured receive threshold, SQS moves it to the DLQ.

consoleSteps.title: Add the SQS trigger

instructions.text: Open the SQS trigger in the Function overview.
Record the event source mapping UUID as [SQS_EVENT_SOURCE_MAPPING_UUID].

consoleSteps.expectedResult: An enabled SQS event source mapping connects the source queue to the Lambda function with batch size 1.
consoleSteps.warning: The function and queue must be in the same Region. Batch size 1 makes the successful and failed-message outcomes easier to observe.

consoleSteps.title: Send and verify a successful SQS message

instructions.text: Open the Monitor tab for fa-lambda-intermediate-processor.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: The successful message is processed and Lambda logs an SQS batch processed JSON message.
consoleSteps.warning: SQS polling is asynchronous. Allow a short delay before checking the log stream.

consoleSteps.title: Send and observe the intentional failing message

instructions.text: Open the function's newest CloudWatch log stream.
Wait for the source queue visibility timeout to expire.
Wait for the second failed receive.
Confirm one message is available in the DLQ.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: The fixed fail message produces Lambda errors and, after the configured retry behavior, appears in fa-lambda-intermediate-dlq.
consoleSteps.warning: Do not repeatedly inspect the source-queue message because viewing a message can contribute to the receive count and alter the exercise timing.

cliSteps.command: aws lambda create-event-source-mapping --function-name fa-lambda-intermediate-processor --event-source-arn [SOURCE_QUEUE_ARN] --batch-size 1 --enabled --profile fa-lambda-intermediate --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: Create the enabled event source mapping. Record the UUID response field as [SQS_EVENT_SOURCE_MAPPING_UUID].
cliSteps.expectedResult: The response contains State Creating or Enabled and a UUID.
cliSteps.warning: Replace [SOURCE_QUEUE_ARN] with the source queue ARN recorded in task 3.

cliSteps.command: aws lambda wait event-source-mapping-enabled --uuid [SQS_EVENT_SOURCE_MAPPING_UUID] --profile fa-lambda-intermediate --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: Wait until the event source mapping is enabled before sending a message.
cliSteps.warning: Replace the UUID with the value returned by create-event-source-mapping.

cliSteps.command: aws sqs send-message --queue-url [SOURCE_QUEUE_URL] --message-body success --profile fa-lambda-intermediate --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: Send the harmless successful training message.
cliSteps.warning: The event source mapping polls asynchronously, so log delivery is not immediate.

tasks.title: Publish an immutable version and create a live alias
tasks.goal: Publish version 1 of the current function configuration and create a live alias pointing to that version.
tasks.whyItMatters: $LATEST is mutable. A published version is an immutable code-and-configuration snapshot, and an alias is a movable pointer that callers can use as a stable deployment reference.

consoleSteps.title: Publish Lambda version 1

instructions.text: Enter Initial intermediate lab release in Version description.
Record the published version number as [PUBLISHED_VERSION].

consoleSteps.expectedResult: An immutable published version exists and its number is recorded as [PUBLISHED_VERSION].
consoleSteps.warning: Do not expect to edit the code or most configuration of a published version.

consoleSteps.title: Create the live alias

instructions.text: Enter Stable training release in Description.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: The live alias points to the published version.
consoleSteps.warning: An alias is a pointer. A later deployment can move it to another published version without changing clients that use the alias ARN.

cliSteps.command: aws lambda publish-version --function-name fa-lambda-intermediate-processor --description 'Initial intermediate lab release' --profile fa-lambda-intermediate --region eu-west-2

cliSteps.expectedResult: The response contains a qualified function ARN and Version 1 for a newly created function.
cliSteps.warning: Publishing identical $LATEST code and configuration again does not create another version.

cliSteps.command: aws lambda create-alias --function-name fa-lambda-intermediate-processor --name live --function-version [PUBLISHED_VERSION] --description 'Stable training release' --profile fa-lambda-intermediate --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: Create the live alias that points to the published version.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The response contains Name live and FunctionVersion [PUBLISHED_VERSION].
cliSteps.warning: Replace [PUBLISHED_VERSION] with the result from publish-version.

tasks.title: Inspect logs and create a Lambda Errors alarm
tasks.goal: Use structured logs to inspect direct, API, and SQS invocations, then create a no-notification alarm for one or more Lambda Errors in one minute.
tasks.whyItMatters: CloudWatch Logs provides per-invocation diagnostic evidence. Lambda emits Errors when function code or the runtime produces an error; this lab's intentional SQS failure provides a safe metric signal for the alarm.

consoleSteps.title: Inspect structured function logs
consoleSteps.expectedResult: The log group contains JSON application logs showing direct, HTTP, successful SQS, and intentional failing SQS processing.
consoleSteps.warning: Log delivery can take several minutes. Refresh the log stream list if the most recent event is not visible yet.

consoleSteps.title: Create the no-notification Errors alarm

instructions.text: Set Datapoints to alarm to 1 out of 1.
Choose Remove for the notification action.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: A no-notification alarm named fa-lambda-intermediate-errors evaluates the Lambda Errors Sum metric over one minute.
consoleSteps.warning: The intentional fail message can make the alarm enter ALARM. This is expected for the lab and does not send a notification.

cliSteps.command: aws logs filter-log-events --log-group-name /aws/lambda/fa-lambda-intermediate-processor --filter-pattern 'Intentional training failure' --profile fa-lambda-intermediate --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: Search the named log group for the controlled failure evidence.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The response eventually includes an event containing Intentional training failure.
cliSteps.warning: Log delivery can take several minutes after invocation.

cliSteps.command: aws cloudwatch put-metric-alarm --alarm-name fa-lambda-intermediate-errors --alarm-description 'Training alarm for Lambda Errors' --namespace AWS/Lambda --metric-name Errors --dimensions Name=FunctionName,Value=fa-lambda-intermediate-processor --statistic Sum --period 60 --evaluation-periods 1 --threshold 1 --comparison-operator GreaterThanOrEqualToThreshold --treat-missing-data notBreaching --profile fa-lambda-intermediate --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: Create an alarm without an alarm action when Errors is at least one during a one-minute period.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The command succeeds without output and the named alarm appears in CloudWatch.
cliSteps.warning: This creates an alarm only; it does not configure email, SNS, or Lambda actions.

verification.title: Confirm log evidence across invocation methods
verification.instruction: Inspect a recent log stream in the named log group.
verification.expectedResult: The log stream contains structured messages produced by the direct, API, and SQS handler paths.

verification.title: Confirm alarm configuration
verification.instruction: Open fa-lambda-intermediate-errors in CloudWatch Alarms.
verification.expectedResult: The metric is AWS/Lambda Errors with FunctionName fa-lambda-intermediate-processor, Sum, one-minute period, and threshold greater than or equal to one.

tasks.title: Perform reverse-dependency cleanup

findings.message: The exact AWS Console layout can change. In particular, API Gateway HTTP API creation screens may present the Lambda integration during API creation or after selecting the API; retain the fixed resource names, route GET /area, stage lab, and Lambda integration target.

The local AWS CLI profile is not an AWS Console resource. Its final cleanup uses local-file instructions plus four independent aws configure unset commands because AWS CLI profile removal is local configuration management.

The SQS failure exercise timing depends on polling and the configured 120-second source queue visibility timeout. The fail message can take several minutes to be delivered twice and appear in the DLQ.
